description: Comparative analysis of three high-performance DEFLATE decompression implementations: libdeflate, zlib-ng, and Intel ISA-L.

libdeflate.language: C with BMI2 target attribute dispatch

hot_loop_structure.design: Two-loop: fastloop (no bounds checks) + generic loop (safe tail)
hot_loop_structure.fastloop_entry: Branchless refill -> preload litlen entry -> test literal bit -> decode up to 3 literals inline -> if match: extract length+distance -> word-at-a-time copy
hot_loop_structure.latency_hiding: Next table preload issued before current match copy executes; saved_bitbuf avoids extra bit consumption steps
hot_loop_structure.multi_symbol: Up to 3 literals per fastloop iteration on 64-bit platforms

table_sizes.dynamic_table_bits: Yes - litlen table bits reduced when max code length < 11

optimizations: Branchless 64-bit bit buffer refill (OR-based bitsleft update, no branches)
BMI2 BZHI instruction for variable-width bit extraction on Haswell+
Multi-symbol decode: up to 3 literals from single refill
Packed 32-bit table entries (symbol + length + extra bits in one u32)
Word-at-a-time match copy with special cases for distance=1 (RLE), distance<8
Five unconditional word stores for match copies before loop
saved_bitbuf pattern for extracting extra bits without separate consume step
Table construction via incremental doubling (cache-friendly)
Dynamic litlen table_bits to shrink table when codes are short
Whole-buffer API only (no streaming overhead)
libdeflate.simd_usage: None in decode loop. Word-at-a-time scalar copies only. SSE/AVX used for CRC32/Adler32 checksums.

zlib_ng.language: C with SIMD intrinsics (SSE2, AVX2, NEON, VSX)

hot_loop_structure.design: Modified zlib inflate_fast() with optimized bit handling
hot_loop_structure.key_changes: Unconditional refill (from dougallj contributions), literal fastpath, optimized chunkset copies

table_sizes.note: Smaller tables than libdeflate, inherited from zlib's conservative design

optimizations: SIMD-accelerated chunkset for match copies (SSE2/AVX2 16/32-byte chunks)
Unconditional bit buffer refill (contributed by dougallj)
Literal fastpath for runs of literal-only symbols
SIMD inflate match copy with chunkmemset for short distances
Compare256 functions using SIMD for string matching (compression)
Slide hash using SIMD (compression)
Maintains full zlib API compatibility (streaming, dictionary, etc.)
zlib_ng.simd_usage: SSE2/AVX2 for match copies in inflate. SIMD heavily used in compression path (hash, match, slide).

throughput.note: Decompression is not the primary optimization focus; zlib-ng focuses more on compression speed

intel_isal.language: Hand-coded x86-64 NASM assembly with C fallback

hot_loop_structure.design: Speculative write pattern in assembly: write symbols as literals speculatively, branch back only for common case (literal)
hot_loop_structure.dispatch: Multi-binary dispatch: base(C) -> SSE2(_01) -> BMI2(_04) via mbin_dispatch_init5
hot_loop_structure.multi_symbol: Decode 1-3 symbols per lookup (sym_count field in table entry). Triple-symbol for blocks >4KB, double for >2KB, single for small blocks.
hot_loop_structure.pipeline: Speculative next-lookup preloaded before current symbol is fully processed; read_in reload overlapped with decode

table_sizes.expanded_length_entries: Yes - length codes include extra bits in table, eliminating separate extra-bits read

optimizations: Hand-coded x86-64 assembly for hot loop (not compiler-generated)
Multi-symbol Huffman decode: up to 3 literals per single table lookup (12-bit primary table)
BMI2: SHRX/SHLX for variable shifts without cl register, BZHI for bit extraction
SSE2 MOVDQU for 16-byte unaligned match copies
Doubling strategy for overlapping match copies (distance < 16)
Speculative literal write before testing if symbol is actually a literal
Pre-generated static Huffman tables detected and loaded via memcpy (skip parsing)
Expanded lit/len table: length extra bits folded into table entries
Input reload (read_in) overlapped with decode computation
intel_isal.simd_usage: SSE2 MOVDQU for match copies only. BMI2 scalar instructions (SHRX, SHLX, BZHI) for decode. No SIMD for Huffman decoding itself.

throughput.note: Hand-coded assembly extracts maximum IPC from the serial decode chain

rows: Clean C, portable, fast table build

key_takeaways_for_our_design: libdeflate's approach is the most practical starting point: pure C with architecture dispatch, ~1100 MB/s, clean codebase.
ISA-L's 12-bit primary table with 3-symbol entries shows that wider tables with multi-symbol packing is the proven best strategy.
Neither libdeflate nor ISA-L uses SIMD for the actual Huffman decode step - both are scalar. This confirms the serial dependency is the true bottleneck.
zlib-ng's lower decompression speed (735 MB/s) vs libdeflate/ISA-L is largely due to smaller tables (9-bit) and no multi-symbol decode.
The ~1100 MB/s ceiling on Silesia suggests that single-threaded x86-64 DEFLATE decode is memory-bandwidth-limited at ~1 GB/s for typical compressible data.

Our target of 2x over zlib-ng (1470+ MB/s) requires surpassing libdeflate/ISA-L by ~33%. This is aggressive but possible via: (a) zero-refill bit reader (dougallj), (b) two-pass architecture, (c) AVX2 copy acceleration beyond SSE2.
